key_test: Welch two-sample t-test of implicit preference imppref (sign-aligned IAT D), new-pair raters (rateorig 0) vs original-pair raters (rateorig 1), immediate session
exclusions: exppref NA (322), d NA (285), fastpct10 == 1 (1), alltrials != 200 (62), applied in that order
notes: Key test is the implicit one (the report names it the single key result; d=.21 and df=3511.1 match only it). The script prints the explicit test first (t=-22.77, d=.75 pooled / .76 by 2t/sqrt(df)). DV check: imppref equals the IAT D score sign-flipped where reemgood is true, rebuilt for all 3597 rows. The script's exclusions screen on d (raw D) and exppref, not on imppref; no imppref NA remains. rateorig 0 = new pair, so t is new minus original. The final dataset was not rebuilt from the 88 MB raw IAT trials. R ran in full (Hmisc and psych present).
